subject: SLA alignment & evidence handoff — Order Form redlines
messages:
From: Sam Patel <sam@stellarpay.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Linda Moore <linda.moore@stellarpay.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SLA & maintenance windows — redlines for Order Form

Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — StellarPay is excited to move forward. Our procurement and SRE teams reviewed the draft order form and attached our redlines (Stellar_SLA_Redlines_v2.docx). A few items we want to surface before the legal sync: 

- Uptime target: Our procurement team is asking to move the baseline uptime to 99.95% for the dedicated cluster. Current draft lists 99.9% — can Redwood accommodate 99.95% or provide a higher credit multiplier?
- Service credits: We need a clear cap and a definition for recurring incidents (we typically escalate after 3 incidents in a 90-day window).
- P1 response: We requested a 4-hour initial response for P1 incidents and a 24-hour remediation estimate. Is that acceptable?
- Maintenance windows: StellarPay has global traffic spikes between 02:00–06:00 ET. We asked for a blackout against rolling maintenance during that period and any weighty infrastructure changes outside a 7-day notification.
- Evidence & audit: We will require an evidence pack for any credit claim (uptime graphs, KV cache logs, relevant runbook excerpts). Please confirm Redwood's turnaround time for sharing evidence (we requested 3 business days).

Can we set a brief call Monday to walk through these redlines and get alignment before legal starts redlining the MSA?

Thanks,
Sam Patel
Head of Platform Reliability
StellarPay

Attachment: Stellar_SLA_Redlines_v2.docx (docx, 48KB)
From: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Patel <sam@stellarpay.com>
Cc: jonas_weber <jonas@redwood.ai>, connor_obrien <connor@redwood.ai>, Linda Moore <linda.moore@stellarpay.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 13:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA & maintenance windows — redlines for Order Form

Sam — appreciate the clear list and the doc. I've attached our initial counter (Redwood_SLA_Proposal_v1.docx) with suggested compromises. High level: 

- Uptime: We can consider 99.95% for the dedicated pool if StellarPay agrees to a tiered credit ladder and commits to a 12-month reserved capacity baseline. Otherwise, 99.9% is our standard for shared capacity.
- Credits cap: Redwood prefers a monthly cap equal to 100% of one month’s hosted fees (we've proposed a 3-tier cap in the attached).
- P1 response: We can commit to a 4-hour acknowledgement and a 24-hour initial remediation plan for P1s with dedicated SLAs for dedicated clusters.
- Maintenance windows: We can accept blackout windows for rolling maintenance between 02:00–06:00 ET. We propose a single 6-hour rolling maintenance window per quarter as carveout; any additional blackouts can be scheduled with 7-day notice.
- Evidence turnaround: Ops can provide preliminary uptime graphs within 3 business days; full runbook excerpts and logs may require up to 7 business days depending on the scope.

Looping in Jonas (legal) and Connor (ops) to put concrete language around credits, escalation, and the evidence pack requirements so we can present a single redline to your team on Monday. Would 10:00 AM ET work for a 30-minute call?

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0192

Attachment: Redwood_SLA_Proposal_v1.docx (docx, 35KB)
From: jonas_weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, connor_obrien <connor@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 11 Sep 2026 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: RE: SLA & maintenance windows — legal annotations

Marissa / Connor — quick legal read-through from my side, attached as an annotated text (Redwood_Legal_SLA_annotated.txt). Key items we should present as options rather than a single take: 

- Credit cap: I support a cap (100% of one month) but want an explicit exclusion for credits triggered by customer misconfiguration or third-party outages. We should add a definition section for "Service Unavailability" that references Redwood's monitoring and incident classification.
- Recurring incidents: propose an escalation to executive review (both parties) after 3 P1 incidents in a rolling 90-day window, with remediation milestones tied to credit multipliers.
- Evidence: 3 business days for preliminary uptime charts is reasonable, but we should require 5 business days to provide consolidated evidence for complex incidents. Also include a privilege-preserving clause for any logs that redacts customer data (we cannot disclose PII).
- Maintenance carveouts: Accept blackout for 02:00–06:00 ET but add permissive language for emergency maintenance with 24-hour notice where applicable. Also propose a one-time migration carveout (up to 8 hours) during onboarding if agreed in writing.

Ask: Marissa, do you want me to convert these notes into redline language for the MSA and order form, or should I instead prepare a short memo with the two-tier options (customer-favored vs Redwood-favored) to take to the call? I can have the redline ready by end of day if you prefer.

Jonas Weber
Sr. Counsel, Redwood Inference
jonas@redwood.ai

Attachment: Redwood_Legal_SLA_annotated.txt (text, 12KB)
From: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Patel <sam@stellarpay.com>, Linda Moore <linda.moore@stellarpay.com>

Date: Fri, 11 Sep 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA & maintenance windows — redlines for Order Form

Thanks Sam — looping back with legal and ops feedback and a suggested path to resolution.

On Fri, Sep 11, 2026 at 9:30 AM, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Marissa / Connor — quick legal read-through from my side, attached as an annotated text (Redwood_Legal_SLA_annotated.txt). Key items we should present as options rather than a single take: 
> 
> - Credit cap: I support a cap (100% of one month) but want an explicit exclusion for credits triggered by customer misconfiguration or third-party outages.

Summary of where we landed (see attachments for details):
- Uptime: Redwood can offer 99.95% for a Dedicated Pool tied to a 12-month reserved commitment. For shared deployments, 99.9% remains standard.
- Credits: Cap at one month’s fees (standard), with exclusions for customer-caused outages and third-party infra incidents. We propose a 3-tier credit ladder in the order form to address severity and recurrence.
- P1 response: 4-hour acknowledgement + 24-hour initial remediation plan for Dedicated Pools.
- Evidence: Ops will provide preliminary charts within 3 business days, consolidated evidence within 5 business days for complex incidents. Logs will be redacted for PII / customer data.
- Maintenance: Accept blackout 02:00–06:00 ET for rolling maintenance. Emergency maintenance allowed with 24-hour notice; onboarding migration carveout (one-time, up to 8 hours) to be scheduled in writing.

Next steps: 
1) Jonas can push these edits to the MSA/order form redline today — I will attach the redline to the HubSpot deal record and share the DocuSign preview link. 
2) Propose a 30-min sync: Monday 10/12 10:00 AM ET (alternate 2:00 PM ET) — please confirm which works for StellarPay.
3) If you’re comfortable, I’ll send the DocuSign preview link and the revised order form so procurement can circulate internally.

Sam / Linda — happy to walk through each bullet on Monday. If you’d prefer Jonas to produce two redline options (customer-friendly vs. standard), let me know and he’ll have those ready.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
